subject: science
passage: The American pika, a small, round-eared relative of rabbits, lives on rocky mountain slopes in western North America, where snow can cover the ground for more than half the year. Unlike marmots and many other mountain mammals, pikas do not hibernate. Instead, they spend the short summer gathering grasses and wildflowers, carrying them mouthful by mouthful to piles hidden beneath boulders. These stores, known as haypiles, supply the food a pika lives on during the long months when it stays active under the snow.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Pikas collect more summer food than any other mountain mammal.
choices.B: Pikas carry grasses and wildflowers to hidden piles beneath boulders.
choices.C: Like marmots, pikas spend the winter hibernating beneath boulders.
choices.D: Pikas stay active all winter by living on food they stored in summer.

explanation.why: The text contrasts pikas with mammals that hibernate: pikas "do not hibernate" but instead gather plants in summer, and these haypiles feed them while they stay "active under the snow." The main idea must connect the summer gathering to winter survival without hibernation.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text never compares how much food pikas and other mammals collect.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This describes how pikas gather food but leaves out why it matters, which is surviving the winter while active.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says that, unlike marmots, pikas do not hibernate.
explanation.D: Correct. This links the whole text: pikas skip hibernation and rely on summer haypiles to stay active through winter.
